introduction: This advanced level explores the mathematical metrics used to evaluate the financial strength and reliability of an insurance company, along with macro-economic indicators.

core_concepts.title: Claim Settlement Ratio (CSR)
core_concepts.description:
It shows how many claims the company passed out of every 100 claims it received. 
Formula: $CSR = (\frac{\text{Total Claims Approved}}{\text{Total Claims Received}}) \times 100$ 
(A higher CSR indicates a highly reliable and customer-friendly company).

core_concepts.title: Incurred Claim Ratio (ICR)
core_concepts.description:
Used mainly in General Insurance. It indicates the total amount of money paid as claims against the total premium earned by the company. 
If ICR is greater than 100%, it means the company is paying out more in claims than it is earning in premiums (making an operational loss).

core_concepts.title: Solvency Ratio
core_concepts.description: This indicates the 'financial strength' of the company to settle all future claims, even in a worst-case scenario (like a natural disaster). IRDAI mandates that all insurance companies in India must maintain a minimum Solvency Ratio of '1.5' (or 150%).

core_concepts.title: Bancassurance
core_concepts.description: It is a partnership model where a Bank sells the insurance policies of an Insurance Company through its own branch network. This has been the most successful distribution channel to increase insurance reach in rural India.

important_entities.name: Insurance Penetration vs. Density
important_entities.significance:
1. Penetration: Total insurance premium collected measured as a 'Percentage of GDP'. 
2. Density: Total insurance premium collected divided by the total population (measured in 'USD per capita').

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A massive trap for banking exams: CSR is based on the 'Number' of claims approved. ICR is based on the 'Monetary Value' of the claims paid versus premium earned. Do not interchange their definitions.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A Solvency ratio below 1.5 triggers strict regulatory action by IRDAI to prevent the company from going bankrupt.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC frequently tests the difference between Insurance Penetration and Density. Remember: Penetration = GDP%, Density = Per Capita Money.
